# Sheet template (optional)

Strecke reads any Google Sheet that has a column named `word` (or `Wort`). This template is a convenience: it has every column the app understands, notes on each header, dropdowns for the fixed lists, an example row, and the optional Inbox and Meta tabs. Column rules: [SHEET_SCHEMA.md](../SHEET_SCHEMA.md).

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `strecke-template.xlsx` | All four tabs in one file: *Read me*, *Words*, *Inbox*, *Meta* |
| `Words.csv`, `Inbox.csv`, `Meta.csv`, `Read-me.csv` | The same tabs as separate CSV files, for importing one at a time |

The files are generated by `python3 tools/template/make_template.py` and checked by `core/test/sheet.test.ts`. They contain one synthetic example row and nothing else.

Nothing is created in your Google Drive by the app or by this repository. You make your own copy.

## Make your own copy

1. Download `strecke-template.xlsx` from this folder.
2. Open [Google Drive](https://drive.google.com), choose **New › File upload**, and pick the file.
3. Right-click the uploaded file and choose **Open with › Google Sheets**.
4. In Sheets, choose **File › Save as Google Sheets**. You now have a normal Google Sheet; the uploaded `.xlsx` can be deleted.

This follows Google's help page [Use both Excel & Sheets: Best practices](https://support.google.com/docs/answer/9331167), which also describes the other route: in an open spreadsheet, **File › Import › Upload**, then *Create new spreadsheet*.

Notes on the header cells and the dropdowns (article, pos, source, verified) should survive the import. Google's help does not promise this for every Excel feature, so if a dropdown is missing, nothing breaks: the app accepts free text and reads it tolerantly.

Then connect the sheet in the app: **Settings › Data**. Follow the numbered steps there. In short: **File › Share › Publish to web**, choose only the Words tab, choose **Comma-separated values (.csv)**, click **Publish**, and paste the link. Google's help page: [Make Google Docs, Sheets, Slides & Forms public](https://support.google.com/docs/answer/183965). Use a computer for this step; the menu wording may differ slightly.

**Publish only the Words tab** (and Inbox, if you use it), never the entire document. Anyone with a published link can read that tab. You can stop publishing at any time from the same dialog.

## Already have a word list? Migrate without breaking anything

You do not need to start over, rename your tab, or use the template's column order.

1. **Make sure one column is called `word`** (or `Wort`, `German`, `Deutsch`, `Lemma`). That is the only requirement.
2. **Name the meaning column** `meaning` (or `English`, `Bedeutung`, `Übersetzung`). Rows without a meaning are listed in the app as needing attention and are not practised until filled.
3. **Add any other columns you want, anywhere**, with the names in [SHEET_SCHEMA.md](../SHEET_SCHEMA.md). Each one adds exercises. Columns the app does not know are ignored, so your own columns (notes, tags, colours) can stay.
4. **Optional tabs:** add a tab named `Inbox` with the headers `word`, `note`, `processed`, and a tab named `Meta` with `schema_version` and `1` in two cells. Missing tabs are fine.
5. **Keep your progress when renaming words:** if you expect to edit the German word itself, add an `id` column with any short unique text per row (for example 1, 2, 3, …). Without an `id`, a renamed word starts fresh in the app. Edits to every other column keep the progress.
6. Publish the words tab as CSV and connect it (above). The app lists, neutrally, any row it reads differently than you might expect ("Row 12 · Schrank: article missing"). Fix those in the sheet whenever you like; they sync on the next open.

Things the app is tolerant about:
- an article written in the word cell (`der Tisch`) or as `m`/`f`/`n`;
- German dates (`11.10.2026`);
- `source` written as `Claude`, `ChatGPT`, `AI` or `ich`;
- empty cells and a title row above the header.
